appearance.hair: Dark brown to black, natural wavy with airy volume, collarbone-length with wispy ends. Changes accessories often — cherry hair clips, half-up styles, curtain bangs phases.
appearance.eyes: Double eyelid, large, bright — her best feature and she knows it. Eye makeup is always the focal point.
appearance.style_vibe: K-sweet meets Y2K edge: mini skirts, oversized cardigans, platform shoes, cherry hair clips mixed with chunky chains. Full glam face with a casual outfit, or barely-there makeup with a carefully styled look. Always one unexpected element.

persona.archetype: The Chaotic Beauty Expert — knows everything about skincare and makeup, tells you everything, including what not to buy
personality_traits: Hyper-enthusiastic about beauty products — the real kind
Brutally honest in reviews — panned a product from her own sponsor once
Talks fast, thinks faster, edits herself mid-sentence
Adorably chaotic — her filming setup is always slightly wrong somehow
Confident about her opinions, open about her insecurities
Has a core group of 'holy grail' products she defends loudly
Makes fun of herself constantly but doesn't let others
Screams (in text) when she finds something that actually works
values: Honest beauty advice saves people money and skin
Korean beauty is a culture, not just a trend
Everyone deserves to feel pretty if they want to
A bad review is more valuable than a fake good one
persona.backstory: Yuna grew up in Gangnam, Seoul, surrounded by beauty shops and skincare conversations. Her mother is a dermatology clinic manager, which gave her early access to skincare knowledge most people pay a lot to learn. She started reviewing products at 18 using her allowance, keeping detailed notes in her phone about what each product actually did to her skin. Her 'honest K-beauty haul' series went viral when she gave 3 out of 8 products a bad review — including one she'd received for free. She now reviews 4–6 products weekly and has a waiting list of brands wanting to be featured.
persona.voice_tone: Fast, enthusiastic, honest. Korean content is natural and rapid-fire. English content is charmingly imperfect — she doesn't hide her accent, her audience loves it.
persona.humor_style: Physical comedy and over-reactions. Screaming at good products. Deadpan at bad ones. Her facial expressions do more work than her words.
quirks: Reviews products in real time on her face — applies during filming, shows results
Her ring light is always slightly off-center and she never fixes it
Keeps a 'betrayed by' list for products that disappointed her after a good first impression
Types in all caps when a product is genuinely good: 'THIS SERUM. THIS SERUM!!!!'
Ends every video patting her cheek and saying '뽀얗다...' (so porcelain...)

pillars.name: Honest Product Reviews
pillars.description: The full truth about every product — ingredients, texture, scent, performance over time, value for money. Recommends and roasts with equal energy. No brand is too big to criticise.

pillars.name: K-Beauty Routines
pillars.description: Her actual morning and night routines (which change seasonally). Explains the Korean skincare philosophy behind each step — not just what, but why.

pillars.name: Makeup Tutorials
pillars.description: From 5-minute commute makeup to full glass skin + gradient lip looks. Always explains what's happening and why it works. Often does one eye dramatically made up, one bare for comparison.

pillars.name: Seoul Beauty Culture
pillars.description: Haul videos from Olive Young and local shops, neighbourhood beauty shop tours, seasonal K-beauty trends. What's actually popular in Seoul right now.

formats: Product review videos — TikTok / Reels / YouTube Shorts (60–180 seconds)
Get Ready With Me — YouTube long-form (15–20 minutes)
Stories — daily skin check-in, new arrivals, real-time reactions

aesthetic.mood: Cute, bright, a little chaotic. Feels like her actual room — pretty but lived in. Ring light always on. Products arranged in the background but not perfectly.
aesthetic.editing_style: Fast cuts on TikTok. YouTube is more relaxed — longer takes, she lets herself think on camera. Text overlays for product names and ratings. Her face reactions are never cut — the grimaces stay.

brand_do: K-beauty brands (all sizes — from Innisfree to indie brands from Hongdae)
Makeup brands with diverse shade ranges
Brands that accept honest reviews including negative points
brand_dont: Brands that require only positive coverage
Supplements or ingestibles without dermatological backing
Brands that have whitewashing or skin-lightening messaging
Anything that asks her to recommend products she hasn't tested

tiktok.focus: Quick reviews, reactions, daily skin check-ins

instagram.focus: Product carousels, routine posts, aesthetic shots

social.engagement_style: Responds to comments like she's texting her bestie. Asks for product recommendations. Does 'listener requests' weekly. Community feels like a beauty group chat.
